hints.title: Problem Analysis
hints.text: Sort transactions chronologically per user using ROW_NUMBER() over (partition by user_id order by transaction_date).

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Use lag(spend, 1) and lag(spend, 2) to inspect the spend amounts of the preceding two transactions.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy
hints.text: Filter for row number 3 where current spend is strictly greater than both previous spends.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH RankedTransactions AS (
    SELECT 
        user_id,
        spend AS third_transaction_spend,
        transaction_date AS third_transaction_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS rn,
        LAG(spend, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS prev1,
        LAG(spend, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS prev2
    FROM Transactions
)
SELECT 
    user_id,
    third_transaction_spend,
    third_transaction_date
FROM RankedTransactions
WHERE rn = 3 
  AND third_transaction_spend > prev1 
  AND third_transaction_spend > prev2
ORDER BY user_id ASC;
```

        spend AS third_transaction_spend,

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS rn,

import pandas as pd

def find_third_transaction(transactions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = transactions.sort_values(by=['user_id', 'transaction_date']).copy()
    df['rn'] = df.groupby('user_id').cumcount() + 1
    df['prev1'] = df.groupby('user_id')['spend'].shift(1)
    df['prev2'] = df.groupby('user_id')['spend'].shift(2)
    res = df[(df['rn'] == 3) & (df['spend'] > df['prev1']) & (df['spend'] > df['prev2'])].copy()
    res = res.rename(columns={'spend': 'third_transaction_spend', 'transaction_date': 'third_transaction_date'})
    return res[['user_id', 'third_transaction_spend', 'third_transaction_date']].sort_values(by='user_id')
